data.title: FRMI Stock Clocks Best Day Ever After Report Names Amazon As Project Matador Customer
data.description:
Key points:
  • On Thursday, Fermi said the hyperscaler is advancing an initial 600 MW of power capacity beginning in 2027.
  • No definitive long-term lease has been signed; the customer is committing capital ahead of a lease to secure power within its targeted timeline, the company said.
  • Fermi said it plans to mobilize on site by December 1 and targets initial power in late second quarter or early third quarter of 2027.

Shares of Fermi Inc. (FRMI) extended their rebound on Friday, clocking their best day ever, and building on a sharp Thursday advance after the company disclosed major commitments from an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for 600 megawatts of power capacity at its Project Matador campus near Amarillo, Texas.

The Financial Times on Friday reported that people familiar with the matter identified the customer as Amazon, marking a reversal of earlier investment talks that collapsed last December. Amazon is expected to build its own data centers on the site, according to the people cited by the FT.

FRMI shares closed up 26% on Friday on the report.

Hyperscaler Commitments And Site Progress

Fermi is a pre-revenue developer of large-scale AI data-center campuses with dedicated on-site power. Co-founded in early 2025 by former U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry and energy financier Toby Neugebauer, it went public in October 2025 with a pitch for the world’s largest such campus.

On Thursday, Fermi said an investment-grade hyperscaler is advancing an initial 600 MW of power capacity at Project Matador beginning in 2027. The customer has agreed to a $200 million prepayment, a $15 million early construction and site-development agreement, and the two sides are finalizing a $90 million purchase of structural steel and building materials Fermi had already secured. No definitive long-term lease has been signed; the company said the customer is committing capital ahead of a lease to secure power within its targeted timeline.

Fermi said it plans to mobilize on site by December 1 and targets initial power in late second quarter or early third quarter of 2027.

FRMI’s Tough Road

FRMI shares have dived from their post-IPO peak amid financing concerns and the collapse of earlier tenant talks, including with Amazon and Oracle. Founder Neugebauer was ousted in April after allegations that his conduct damaged customer relations. Fermi still needs to secure project financing and satisfy conditions on its 99-year land lease with Texas Tech University by year-end, while its air permits face court challenges.

On Thursday, the company reported third-quarter net loss of $141.6 million and said it ended September with $286.3 million in cash against roughly $958 million in debt. It also said that it has terminated its earlier lease with neocloud TensorWave, signed in August.

How Did FRMI Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around FRMI stock jumped from 'bullish' to 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'high' levels.

A Stocktwits user said the deal is “just the beginning” for Fermi.

Another user opined that the deal just “saved the company.”

data.title: Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Q3 Revenue Rises 883% to $3.56 Million
data.description:
Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.56 million, up 883% year over year, following the expansion of its international trading business. Gross profit was $281,407, while the company recorded an operating loss of $821,890 and a net loss from continuing operations of $2.55 million. The net loss included a $2.78 million expense from a change in the fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $3,557,805, compared with $361,935 a year earlier, an increase of 883.0%.
  • Gross profit was $281,407, compared with $44,178 in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Operating loss was $821,890, down from $1,564,479 a year earlier.
  • Net loss from continuing operations was $2,547,995, compared with $1,314,650 in the prior-year quarter.
  • For the first nine months of 2026, revenue was $4,519,414 and net loss from continuing operations was $3,093,215.

Business Highlights

  • International trading became the company’s primary revenue-generating segment in the quarter. All segment revenue was generated by Super International Trading, acquired on May 27, 2026.
  • The logistics and warehousing segment reported no revenue in the quarter, following Edward’s disposition and the expiration of TWEW’s legacy customer service contracts.
  • TWEW is renegotiating logistics and labor service arrangements with customers from before its acquisition; letters of intent and draft contracts with certain customers are being executed.
  • The company said it is focused on strengthening its international trading operations, expanding business opportunities, optimizing its operating structure and improving operational efficiency.

data.title: Beasley Broadcast Group Posts Q3 Revenue of $42.8 Million, Net Loss of $12.1 Million
data.description:
Beasley Broadcast Group reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $42.8 million, down 16.1% year over year, and a net loss of $12.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.3 million, compared with $3.9 million in the prior-year quarter. The company cited advertising weakness and highlighted cost reductions, local direct advertising growth, and improved digital operating margins.

Financial Highlights

  • Net revenue was $42.8 million for the quarter, compared with $51.0 million a year earlier.
  • Operating loss was $12.8 million, versus an operating loss of $0.5 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net loss was $12.1 million, or $6.52 per diluted share, compared with a net loss of $3.6 million, or $1.97 per diluted share.
  • Adjusted EBITDA was $1.3 million, down from $3.9 million in the prior-year quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Local direct revenue increased 7% year over year on a same-station basis, partly offsetting weakness in traditional national and local agency advertising.
  • Digital revenue declined 12.3% year over year on a same-station basis during the quarter, while year-to-date same-station digital revenue rose 4.4%.
  • The digital segment’s operating margin was 32%, compared with 21% a year earlier; management attributed the improvement to progress toward a more efficient, higher-margin digital business.
  • Beasley continued its focus on rebuilding core revenue, improving sales productivity, expanding digital profitability, and reducing leverage. Following quarter-end, it completed the sale of two radio stations and two real estate parcels.
